svg.title: TOPAK B11 — The Build-Run pipeline: one ordered path from intake to rollout, keyed by digest; Run's output re-enters only through intake and enables nothing; a carrier moves objects and decides nothing
svg.desc: ADR-0069 (Proposed, 2026.11.12, revised R1 to R3 the same day; C1 to C4 attach) joins the steps that ADR-0024, ADR-0021, ADR-0044 and ADR-0031 decide into nine stages, each taking only the digest the stage before produced. Two stages are new: intake (§3, gated by §3a) and signing for every promoted class (§7). Authority runs one way; what Run produces returns as data through intake and enables nothing until a promotion. Git and GitHub are guidance (§10). Nothing here is modelled or checked, no module is written, and the reference has no intake, no gate-evidence key, no signing stage and no pipeline around its tally. What is built is stage 4's carrier for this repository: checks, results and sources, which promote nothing during genesis (§10.3). This diagram reads those files at build and compares them with the digests §10.2 states; columns headed as the diagram's are its own.
svg.text: TOPAK · B11

text.tspan: The Build-Run pipeline: one ordered path from intake to rollout, keyed by digest; Run's output re-enters only through intake and enables nothing; a carrier moves objects and decides nothing

svg.text: ADR-0069 (Proposed, 2026.11.12, revised R1 to R3 the same day; C1 to C4 attach) joins the steps that ADR-0024, ADR-0021, ADR-0044 and ADR-0031 decide into nine stages, each taking only the digest the stage before produced. Two stages are new: intake (§3, gated by §3a) and signing for every promoted class (§7). Authority runs one way; what Run produces returns as data through intake and enables nothing until a promotion. Git and GitHub are

guidance (§10). Nothing here is modelled or checked, no module is written, and the reference has no intake, no gate-evidence key, no signing stage and no pipeline around its tally. What is built is stage 4's carrier for this repository: checks, results and sources, which promote nothing during genesis (§10.3). This diagram reads those files at build and compares them with the digests §10.2 states; columns headed as the diagram's are its own.

text.tspan: Not issued · D-0069-2 is today's position
Built: checks, results, sources; promotes nothing (§10.3)
ADR-0024, ADR-0044, ADR-0045, ADR-0033 (restated or resolved)
Seven things the custodian settled (provenance note)

svg.text: ⟨K1⟩ a new record for a Build-Run pipeline, which restates or reverses every earlier Build decision.
⟨K2⟩ generic in requirement, with specific guidance for git and GitHub.
⟨K3⟩ it repurposes f1-tla's CI/CD (three workflows at 5fe66dd).
⟨K4⟩ the pipeline takes in what Run produces, for retraining on experience and as training data.
⟨K5⟩ intake from Run is a special case of intake, in this record.
⟨K6⟩ labelled return is a separate case.
⟨K7⟩ that Run does not adapt is cited and restated, not newly decided.
Every other choice is the drafter's: (drafter's choice) where the alternative was live, (drafter's recommendation) where the custodian was asked and has not answered.

text.tspan: Status note: four criteria attach, and what is built

svg.text: C1: §5 puts a proof obligation on erasure, a privileged path.
C2: §3 claims intake is the only path into a corpus root.
C3: §7 reverses in effect ADR-0016 §1's "Build promotion key" (Annex B, item 1).
C4: it resolves debts of ADR-0033 §1, ADR-0044 §4, ADR-0041 (the Build half) and ADR-0045 §6.
Built (R3): stage 4's carrier for this repository, checks and results, green on pull requests into the record's branch "and not yet on main". Nothing else is modelled,
The reference has a promotion tally (mechanism.rs) and refuses a Vote until gate evidence is recorded (mechanism/ I18), but no pipeline around it, no intake, no
gate-evidence key and no carrier configuration. Pending: none. Deployment position: Archetype.

text.tspan: Four open questions, put 2026.11.12 and not answered (provenance note)

svg.text: The scope (cited as "§10.6"; the record's §10 has §10.1 to §10.3, and no §10.6 exists in it: the diagram's observation).
Whether GitHub is a trust root (§9; Options: not taken, drafter's recommendation).
Whether the CI runner is a principal (§9 C-3; Options: not taken, drafter's recommendation).
Which reversals to make (Annex A).
Also unanswered: every (drafter's choice); the custodian's reading of them all is a §12 item.

text.tspan: is computed from the log by an allowlisted tool in a Build round, never

svg.text: written by a principal. ADR-0035 §1's "projected from the log, not authored", applied to data.
An ordinary Build round; its artifact is the objects with the log positions they derive from. In git, a manifest
change (§10.1). IG-4 reruns the extractor at intake (§3a).
A control-plane fact (ADR-0004), or a record derived only from such facts:
admit decisions (ADR-0028 F1); stop attributions (F2, "a feedback path, not merely evidence"); promotion
votes (F3); Actuate records, by digest (ADR-0042 §3, §4); Observer and correlator findings.
None is erasable, so their return carries no erasure obligation.
A Run item carrying an ADR-0047 label, or a cognitive payload: the task, a Consult's content, an Actuate's
result, a principal's emission. Everything else a Run round holds.

text.tspan: Admitted only when LR-1, LR-2 and LR-3 hold. LR-1 (Build's Listener labels) is undecided, so no

svg.text: labelled return is admitted. Never in git (§10.1).
Run does not adapt ⟨K7⟩: weights, a bundle, a profile or a seating that changed in Run would be one
nobody promoted; the next attestation does not match it and the mechanism refuses the lease (§2).
What Run holds returns to Build as data, and the notation Build(Contain) → Run(Contain) keeps its one
arrow: a return path and no return arrow (§2).
leases naming the promoted, signed revision
the return path: data, not authority; no arrow in the notation (§2). It enables nothing until a round reads it and the
round's artifact passes stages 3 to 8
joins the return (§4)
refused while LR-1 is unmet (§5)
source: run objects, generatedBy projected
(RR-1), admitted as a corpus-root revision

Each solid blue arrow carries one digest, the one the stage before produced. P-1: no stage starts on a name, and a stage refuses a digest the stage before it did not produce. P-3: the stages are not reordered. The grey path is what Run produced, admitted at stage 0 as an object in a corpus-root revision that is itself promoted through stages 1 to 8; so every lap of the loop passes the promotion gate, and the loop adds a path for influence and none for authority (§2, §4). The status pills say what the
reference has: a tally, and nothing around it (Status note).

text.tspan: P-1 · No stage starts on a name

svg.text: It starts on a digest, and refuses one the stage before it did not produce. ADR-0044's "A file name is no longer evidence
of anything", applied to every stage (drafter's choice).

text.tspan: P-2 · A stage's output is a log fact or a signed object

svg.text: Either a log fact or an object signed under an issued key. It is never a carrier's record of a step (§9).

text.tspan: P-3 · The stages are not reordered

svg.text: Gates run before the tally (ADR-0024 §4), signing comes after the tally (ADR-0044 §4). Publication follows signing, and
rollout follows publication.

text.tspan: P-4 · An artifact that stops at any stage has no egress

svg.text: ADR-0039 §3 already holds this for an unsubmitted round: "An authoring round that is never submitted has no egress". The
table restates; the new decisions are stage 0 and the rules for stages 4, 6 and 7.

text.tspan: §2 · Authority runs one way; what Run produces returns as data and enables nothing ⟨K4⟩ ⟨K7⟩

svg.text: Build(Contain) → Run(Contain), with the arrow as authority flow (ADR-0001). This record adds no arrow. A Run→Build arrow would say that Run grants Build
authority, and no record allows that (Context).

text.tspan: Restated: Run does not adapt ⟨K7⟩. Five accepted clauses settle it

svg.text: ADR-0015: "Authority changes: exactly {promotion, anchor issuance}".
ADR-0024 §1: "Any artifact crossing from Build to Run requires promotion."
ADR-0034 P5: a Persona's weights are part of the launch measurement.
ADR-0034 P7: a change to either reference value is "a new profile, and so a promotion".
ADR-0034 P6: "Nothing survives except through Submit and Emit"; the Run profile carries it over (ADR-0034 A2).

text.tspan: Learning from Run happens in a Build round, on data that intake admitted, and reaches Run only by promotion.

svg.text: What Run produced enters Build only as an object admitted to a corpus root by intake (§4, §5). It enables nothing until a round reads it and the round's artifact passes
stages 3 to 8.
Every lap of the loop passes the promotion gate, so the loop adds no path for authority. What it adds is a path for influence, and §4 and §5 bound that.

text.tspan: §3 · Intake is the only way into a corpus root ⟨K5⟩: a corpus-root revision is a Build artifact, promoted under ADR-0024 like any other
The decision, and the drafter's choice

svg.text: Its content is a manifest with one line per object. Nothing else changes what a round may Read. This answers the Build half of ADR-0041's open obligation, and
agrees with ADR-0054's sentence on the corpus root (Proposed).
(Drafter's choice: intake is a promotion. The alternative, an operator's attributed act, is in Options. Not taken because a corpus root decides the ingress of every round that
pins it, and so the lineage of everything those rounds produce; ADR-0022 §3 calls the root "the syntactic control over ingress".)
The Run root is not decided here. It crosses from Build to Run, so ADR-0024 §1 already requires it to be promoted; whether this manifest form is its form too is left open
(Open obligations).
I-1. An object with no source line is not admitted, and a revision that drops a line drops the object.
I-2. An external source is pinned by digest at admission. A check that an upstream is still served at its pin, and that no newer issue exists, reports and never edits. A
finding against a pin is input to a new intake. This is f1-tla's sources workflow.
I-3. Intake does not judge content. ADR-0022 §3: "Whether the corpus is poisoned is an Observer finding, not an enforcement decision". The intake round's Observer and
the veto seats deny on it (ADR-0024 §5). The gates of §3a check the manifest's form and recompute what can be recomputed; none reads an object for its meaning.

text.tspan: I-4. A cognitive payload (ADR-0004) is admitted only under §5.

svg.text: I-5. A revision is classified against the one in force, by set difference on digests: additions, removals, or both. An addition widens what a round may read, so it is the
intake counterpart of a relaxation. It promotes as any artifact does, and its generatedBy lines feed ADR-0035's exclusion rule, which is monotone in them (drafter's choice).
SHA-256 of the object's bytes. The object's identity, as ADR-0044 §2's revision is a bundle's
One of external (with the upstream identifier and the digest it was pinned at), promoted (with the promotion entry), or run (§4, §5)
The declaration ADR-0035 §1 says is made "at corpus admission", or the projection §4 requires for run
Empty, except under §5

text.tspan: §3a · What gates an intake (R1): seven mechanical gates, each a program named by digest, and the residual no gate checks

svg.text: The vote on an intake opens only when all seven gates below have passed, and each has written evidence that is signed under §6 G-2, or, while D-0069-2 holds, attributed by AttestGates (ADR-0050). They are mechanical, because ADR-0007 bars semantic judgment as an enabling condition. Each is a program named by digest (§6 G-1). The author of an intake is the principal that submits the manifest, and that principal is recused (ADR-0024 §6). ADR-0024 §4's two checks are ADR-0007's gates and bundle ⊑ floor; both are
written for policy artifacts, and on a manifest they would pass on nothing. §6 G-4 says what replaces them for this class.
Every digest in the manifest is in the store, and the stored bytes hash to it
§3 identity
Every object the revision admits has exactly one line, and every line has a source and its generatedBy and curatedBy fields

Every external line has an upstream identifier and the digest it was pinned at. Where the upstream still serves the object, the runner fetches it and the bytes match. Where it does not, the evidence says so and the line stands on its declaration (drafter's choice)

For every source: run object, the allowlisted extractor named by digest is rerun on the cited log positions, and its output has the object's digest. The generatedBy shares are recomputed from the same positions and match
§4 RR-1. Without this gate, "computed, never written" would be a claim the submitter makes
No run object takes input from an entry in the governed store (ADR-0004) or from a labelled item. While §5 LR-1 is unmet, no labelled object passes
Every object's label contains its label in Run. While IG-5 admits no labelled object, this gate is vacuous, and its evidence says so

The additions and removals against the root in force are computed and written, with the lineages whose generatedBy shares change. The gate always passes once its report exists. At tally, an intake classified against a root that is no longer in force is refused and gated again (drafter's choice)
I-5; the grant seats' evidence

text.tspan: IG-7's tally check keeps two intakes from racing

svg.text: Each was classified against the root that was in force when it was gated. If one promotes, the other's report is stale, and the voters would be voting on a difference that no
longer exists.

text.tspan: What no gate checks: poisoning. I-3 leaves the content to the veto seats

svg.text: The Observer's coverage duty is to the seal of the intake round's topics (ADR-0039 §3). The corpus objects are in those topics only as far as the round read them. A
veto seat denies only on what it samples.
The grant seats vote on IG-7's report, not on the data.
The first check of what the data does is Persona verification, at the promotion of a Persona trained on it (ADR-0016). That is after the intake, and after the training.
For a corpus of any size, intake checks where data came from and that it is what it claims to be. It does not check what the data will teach. This is a declared
residual, in the same place ADR-0022 §3 put it, and nothing here narrows it.
Options rejects a content gate on intake: it would make semantic judgment an enabling condition, which ADR-0007 forbids; as a veto seat's tool it is admissible, and it
subtracts only.

text.tspan: §4 · Intake from Run is a case of intake ⟨K5⟩: RR-1 to RR-4, and what this does not bound

svg.text: It names the Personas whose principals' admits produced the source entries, each with its share.
This gives ADR-0035's field a source in Run; that record says its rule "applies to no lineage node
today", because every node is a Build round.

text.tspan: RR-2 · A return is charged to every lineage named in its

svg.text: A successor trained on a cell's record has the cell's Thinker and its Observer both in its lineage.
ADR-0035 §3's exclusion rule then decides what independence that successor can claim.
A deployment that wants two lineages to stay independent admits each lineage's own record to
that lineage's corpus root, and not the other's (drafter's recommendation; ADR-0017 requires "two
independent lineages" at the archetype).

text.tspan: RR-3 · Each object lists the findings recorded against its source rounds

svg.text: So that the intake's veto seats read them. A finding subtracts, as ADR-0007 requires. It is never
a precondition, and its absence is never a grant (drafter's choice).
The source entries keep their own horizon. The returned object is retained as a corpus object: for
the production lifetime of any artifact promoted from a round that read it (ADR-0021 §7). This
lengthens the life of the derived object and never that of the source topic (ADR-0003 A3).

text.tspan: What this does not bound ⟨K4⟩: the residual

svg.text: A Byzantine Run principal can shape the record its successor trains on: within its alphabet, it
chooses what to Consult and what to Actuate. RR-1 and RR-3 make that influence visible and
attributable. Nothing in them makes it harmless.
The trained successor's behavior is checked only by Persona verification, "a required Build gate"
(ADR-0016). ADR-0017's "Thompson applies to the trainer" now applies to Run as one of the
trainer's sources.

text.tspan: §5 · Labelled return is a separate case, and admits nothing until Build labels ⟨K6⟩

svg.text: ADR-0047 §9 leaves it open: "Whether Build's Listener labels is not decided here." A labelled item read by an unlabelled Build
round loses its label at the point it matters; an untrusted item would reach a Build Thinker in the clear.
Until a record decides that Build labels, no labelled return is admitted (drafter's choice). Not decided: §5 admits

text.tspan: LR-2 · The label travels, and only grows

svg.text: An object's label in the corpus root contains its label in Run. An intake may add a name and never remove one (drafter's
choice; the monotone direction ADR-0035 §2 takes for ingress). IG-6 checks it.

text.tspan: LR-3 · Erasure follows the data: the reason C1 attaches

svg.text: Each object names its erasure locus: the sealed topic, or the entry in the governed store (ADR-0004), it came from. An
erasure of that locus (ADR-0006) obliges: a new intake revision without the object; and for every promoted artifact
whose lineage ingress contains it, withdrawal or a declaration. Withdrawal means ending the rounds that name it
(ADR-0031) and refusing grants that name it.
Keyed on ingress, which ADR-0035 §2 allows to over-approximate, not on consumed, which must never over-approximate
and so could miss an artifact (drafter's choice). A proof obligation over a privileged path.
An erasure that removes a payload leaves its F-class facts (ADR-0028 §1). A labelled return removes nothing from the log. In
git, a labelled return is never stored: rewriting history to erase it would be the out-of-band deletion ADR-0006 forbids (§10.1).

text.tspan: §6 · A gate is a program named by digest, and its evidence counts once an issued key signs it

svg.text: Vote is enabled only after the gates pass (ADR-0024 §4): ADR-0007's totality, non-vacuity and
discrimination gates; bundle ⊑ floor (ADR-0010), floor revisions classified mechanically
(ADR-0030 §5); Persona verification (ADR-0016); the declaration check (ADR-0023 §7b).
For a bundle, the gate "reduces to the three ADR-0007 gates plus signing" (ADR-0030).
Gate evidence is recorded by an operator's AttestGates (ADR-0024 A3, ADR-0050): who
asserted it, not whether it is true.

text.tspan: G-1 · A gate is a program in the repository, named by digest

svg.text: It runs the same way by hand and on a carrier. Its evidence is the file it writes, whose digest is
ADR-0024 §3's gate-evidence digest. A results file is never edited by hand; a rerun that
changes anything is a new file (drafter's choice; f1-tla's rule).

text.tspan: G-2 · Evidence counts once a gate-evidence key, carried in the issued rules,

svg.text: ADR-0045 §6's terms for the gate runner: "admissible as a trust root" with "its evidence signed by a
key carried in issued rules, which ADR-0025 §1 (f) can now hold. Until that key exists, T-0045-13 is
excluded". This record names the key; issuing it is an ADR-0025 §1 (f) amendment (Annex B, item

text.tspan: Until the key is issued, T-0045-13 stays excluded and nothing here changes its class

svg.text: (D-0069-2, today's position).

text.tspan: G-3 · A gate that cannot be rerun from its pin is checked for being in step, not

svg.text: The pinned prover is tlapm 7824dab (tools/TLAPS-PIN); its upstream tag now serves another
build, and its binary is pinned for arm64-darwin. No carrier can rerun the proofs with it unless
the deployment hosts that binary. A carrier runs spec/proof-sync.sh and reports which proofs
are stale; the proofs are rerun where the pinned binary is.

text.tspan: G-4 · A vote opens on its own class's gates, and a class with none stated does

svg.text: (Drafter's choice; the alternative is in Options.) ADR-0024 §4 states two checks for every class;
they fit bundles and floors and say nothing about a manifest, a profile or a seating. A gate that says
nothing about an artifact passes it, so the vote would open on nothing.
A class whose row states none waits until a record writes them. Annex B, item 8, carries the
change into ADR-0024 §4.
ADR-0007's three gates; bundle ⊑ floor; signed
ADR-0024 §4; ADR-0030, its bundle row
ADR-0030 §5's gates, and the computed classification
ADR-0007's gates on the rules floor, with an issuance alongside
None. A reproducible build is T-0045-30, a debt
Persona verification. The lineage is computed by the gate, and independence is checked in the tally
ADR-0016; ADR-0035 §1, §4 (Proposed); ADR-0024 A2
None. ADR-0034 states what a profile fixes, not a gate that checks it
None of its own. ADR-0024 A3 records "the gates of §4" as run, and they do not read a seating
ADR-0024 A3
The composition note exists and states its delta. ADR-0058 adds the graph overlay (Proposed)
Not re-read for this revision. ADR-0054 is Proposed

Mechanism code, profiles and seatings cannot promote under this record until a record gives them gates. During genesis, nothing promotes, so nothing waits yet (§6). Consequences: after bootstrap, that blocks every mechanism release until a code gate exists; the custodian may prefer a declared degeneracy (Options).

text.tspan: §7 · The tally is the log's; signing follows it, for every promoted artifact

svg.text: Unanimity over the grant seats; "A timeout is never a grant"; the round stalls without an independent veto seat and without
coverage to the seal (ADR-0024 §2 and A2; ADR-0039 §3).
A vote binds to the triple, and a change of epoch voids votes in flight (ADR-0024 §3).
Author recusal is a mechanism constant (ADR-0024 §6).
Votes are non-erasable; "The authoritative vote is the admit decision in the consensus log" (ADR-0024 §8).
Every vote covers the sealed topic set (ADR-0021 §4).
Reconciled: ADR-0024 §7 (promotion "does not depend on" ADR-0021) and A2 (stalls on ADR-0021 §3's seal) do not
conflict: §7 is where the vote is recorded, A2 is when the tally may complete. No text changes.

text.tspan: Signing, widened to every class: C3

svg.text: ADR-0044 §4: "The bundle key signs the revision that promotion admitted, after the tally and never before it." Every artifact
class promoted under ADR-0024 §1 is signed the same way: bundles; mechanism releases; Personas; profiles; seatings;
corpus-root revisions (§3); workflows, if ADR-0054 is ratified.
Each is signed under an issued key, after its tally (drafter's choice; per-class keys are in Options). This reverses in effect
ADR-0016 §1, whose Persona ID is "Cryptographically signed by the Build promotion key": ADR-0002 A1 struck the single
human key at Build's commit point, and ADR-0025 §1 (f) lists no such key. Annex B, items 1 and 4.

text.tspan: Not built · signing is a script with a secret (ADR-0033 A6)

svg.text: S-1. The signing stage holds the key and nothing else. It recomputes the artifact digest from the bytes, reads the
promotion entry for that digest from the log, and signs only if the entry is there. No author code and no gate runs where the
key is reachable.
S-2. The signature is over the digest, under domain separation, as ADR-0044 §2 has it.

text.tspan: The stronger successor, possible and not taken

svg.text: ADR-0044 noted: no signature at all, with "the mechanism checks the revision against a promotion entry in its own log". This
record makes the promotion entry name the artifact digest. That successor is possible after this record, and it is not taken
here (Options).

text.tspan: §8 · Publishing locates; rollout ends rounds — §9 · A carrier moves objects and decides nothing

svg.text: Publishing places the artifact and its signature where nodes can fetch them by digest. The location is not evidence (P-1). A node verifies the signature under the keys in force (ADR-0044 §3) before it loads anything.

Restated: a new revision reaches a live principal by ending its round, and across the fleet by an epoch fence (ADR-0031). Runtime subtraction is not promotion (ADR-0024 §9). "There is no emergency seat in Build; a promotion is Build's way to add authority"
Restated: the fast path for strictly subtractive bundles stays deferred (ADR-0024, Options).

text.tspan: §9 · What a carrier is, and what it is not

svg.text: A carrier is every system that moves objects between stages or runs gates for an operator: version control, CI runners, artifact hosting.

This record does not make a carrier a trust root (drafter's recommendation). One of the four open questions (provenance note). GitHub as a trust root is in Options, not taken: admitting a provider's identity is an issuance a deployment may make, and would be
declared.

text.tspan: C-1 · A carrier's approval is not a vote, and its merge is not a promotion

svg.text: The facts that count are the log's (ADR-0024 §8) and the issued keys' (§6, §7).

text.tspan: C-2 · A carrier's checks may refuse and never admit

svg.text: A branch rule or a required review is defence in depth: ADR-0044's Options gave OPA's signatures
the same standing, "Acceptable as an additional check".

text.tspan: C-3 · A CI runner is not a principal

svg.text: (Drafter's recommendation.) It holds no Build alphabet; it runs gates on an operator's behalf, and
the operator's AttestGates records the result (ADR-0050). ADR-0022 §6's obligation ("no shell,
no network egress… no path into the artifactory except Submit") binds Build principals, and a
runner has all three. So a runner is in T-0045-13's row and counts only as G-2 allows.

text.tspan: C-4 · Author code never runs where signing or gate-evidence keys are

svg.text: S-1. In GitHub terms, a job that holds a key runs no repository code except S-1's (§10.1, "Should").

text.tspan: C-5 · A carrier's identifiers locate and do not identify

svg.text: A commit hash, a tag or a release name points at an object. The SHA-256 in §3 and ADR-0044 §2
identifies it.

text.tspan: §10 · Git and GitHub ⟨K2⟩ ⟨K3⟩: guidance. Its "should" is advice; what must be done is §1 to §9's. §10.1 maps each generic requirement and says where GitHub stops

svg.text: A manifest file in the repository, changed by pull request
The objects are not in git, only their digests. They go in a content-addressed store
An extraction round whose artifact is a manifest change
The extractor is an allowlisted tool, not a workflow step
Never in git. Rewriting history to erase it would be the out-of-band deletion ADR-0006 forbids
A branch per round, in a worktree the mechanism owns
A Build principal does not run git (ADR-0022: "No shell, no package installation, no network, no git")
The mechanism commits the workspace and opens a pull request naming the artifact digest and the sealed topic-set digest
The pull request is a locator (C-5)
Required status checks: workflows that call repository scripts
A check's green is the carrier's. The evidence file and its signature are what count (G-2)
A workflow artifact, signed in a separate job under the gate-evidence key
GitHub's artifact attestations may be added. They are signed under GitHub's identity and not an issued key, so they meet C-2 and not G-2
A required check, tally, that reads the log's promotion entry for the digest
Reviews, CODEOWNERS and required approvals are defence in depth (C-2). GitHub's ban on approving one's own pull request echoes recusal, which is a mechanism constant
"Dismiss stale approvals when new commits are pushed"
Covers a new artifact digest, not a new rules epoch. The tally check covers both
A job in a protected environment holding the key, triggered on the merged commit, which does only S-1
Environment reviewers approve any-of. They are not a quorum
A release carrying the artifact and <digest>.sig
The tag locates (C-5)
Outside GitHub. Nodes fetch by digest and verify
The epoch fence is the mechanism's
An on-demand workflow that reports and never edits
Workflows declare permissions: contents: read unless a job needs more.
Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA, not by tag. f1-tla pins by tag, and this is the one change to its workflows.
A job that holds a key runs no repository code except S-1's.

text.tspan: §10.3 · The corpus repository during genesis (drafter's recommendation): gate evidence for the custodian, and no promotion

svg.text: TOPAK's own repository runs checks, results and sources as gate evidence for the custodian's ratification and for the reference. During genesis they promote nothing. Genesis ratification is the custodian's (ADR-0029 §2); no roster exists until the ceremony seats one (ADR-0029 §5, step 1); treating the custodian's merge as a promotion would make it D-0024-2, the single signer, entering unannounced, the ground on which ADR-0033 rejected promoting the reference in place.
After bootstrap a record "changes only through promotion" (ADR-0029 §3). The same workflows then become stage 4 of the corpus's own promotions, and tally, sign and publish are added.

text.tspan: A content gate on intake: a classifier or a model screening the corpus for poisoning (R1)

svg.text: Rejected. It would make semantic judgment an enabling condition, which ADR-0007 forbids. As a veto seat's tool it is admissible, and it subtracts only
The path ADR-0033 said did not exist is one object, with each stage's owner named and two stages (intake, and signing for every class) newly decided.
The corpus root gets an admission rule, and lineage's generatedBy gets a source in Run. Retraining on experience becomes a projected, attributable input and not a
side channel. A return from Run is recomputed at intake (IG-4), not taken on the submitter's word (R1).
Every class's vote opens on gates that read that class (G-4), and the classes that have none are named (R1).
A carrier can be replaced without touching a theorem. GitHub is one instance. Every authoritative check is a script the mechanism owns, which the carrier only runs.
f1-tla's working pattern comes home: thin workflows, scripts that run the same by hand, and results that are regenerated and compared, never edited.
Every corpus change is a promotion. A unanimous quorum per intake is slow, and that is the cost of making the root decide ingress.
The return path is a path for influence. §4's residual stands: a Byzantine Run principal shapes its successor's data, and only Persona verification checks the result.
Labelled return waits on another record (LR-1). Until Build labels, retraining on Run payload is not available.
Erasure grows a long tail. An erasure can withdraw promoted artifacts (LR-3): expensive, disruptive, and the honest price of training on erasable data.
CI does not prove. G-3 leaves the proofs to wherever the pinned prover is, and the carrier only says when they are stale.
Intake does not check what data teaches (§3a; R1). The veto seats sample, the grant seats vote on a report, and the first behavioral check is a Persona's verification after
training.
Mechanism code, profiles and seatings cannot promote until their gates are written (G-4; R1). After bootstrap, that blocks every mechanism release until a code gate
exists.
A ratchet tolerates what stands (R3). The job summary lists the standing findings each time, which keeps them visible, and does not make them go away.
The Run root's admission (ADR-0041's other half): whether §3's manifest is its form.
Whether Build's Listener labels (ADR-0047 §9). §5 waits on it.
The custody rows for the artifact keys and the gate-evidence key, in the deployment declaration. ADR-0044's bundle-key row is still undeclared.
Annex B's entries, drafted, with re-pins.
The module of §12, and the reference's intake, extraction tool, tally check and signing stage.
Of the workflows, built (R3), what remains: the workflows on main, and sources run once; rows files for Correlator, Emergency, Labels, Operators and ToolList, so
spec/modules.tsv can list them; the record lint moved to tools/; the contain tests' guest lookup made independent of cargo's layout; the standing findings the ratchets
list: two corpus pins (ADR-0054, ADR-0055), three Lean series, the record lint's four, and the path citations.
Hosting the pinned prover, if a carrier is ever to rerun the proofs (G-3).
Gates for mechanism code, confinement profiles and seatings (G-4), and a reading of ADR-0054 for a workflow's gates (R1).
The seven intake gates as programs, and the extractor IG-4 reruns as an allowlist entry (R1).
Two questions not moved by this record: ADR-0010's "One floor, shared by Build and Run" against ADR-0022's evidence pointing "at per class" (ADR-0041 leaves it
with G5 item 9); and ADR-0012's "the one artifact verified rather than promoted", beside ADR-0010 A2's "Policy-floor tightening is an ordinary promotion".

Vote is enabled only after the gates of the artifact's class pass, as ADR-0069 §6 G-4 lists them, and an artifact whose class has none stated is not promoted. The two checks §4 names remain the gates of a bundle. ADR-0024 is in the bootstrap set

When this record is built, ADR-0033 takes an addendum with the run, as for A6. The header also carries a debt against ADR-0016 (§7 reverses §1's signing key); ADR-0002, ADR-0016 and ADR-0017 (errata owed); ADR-0025 and ADR-0044 (amendments owed); ADR-0024 (§4, an amendment owed; R1); ADR-0035 (an R-revision owed). Resolves debts of ADR-0033, ADR-0044, ADR-0041 and ADR-0045 on ratification, and only as far as Annex B's entries and the reference carry them. Closes nothing.

svg.text: Initial draft. Build and Run are one ordered path, keyed by digest: intake, round, author, submit and seal, gates, tally, sign, publish, roll out. Intake is the only way into a corpus root and is a promotion. Run's output returns only through intake, as projected control-plane facts or, once Build labels, as labelled payload whose erasure

reaches every artifact with it in ingress. Gate evidence counts once an issued key signs it. Every promoted class is signed after its tally, which reverses in effect ADR-0016 §1's promotion key. A carrier decides nothing. Guidance for git and GitHub, with f1-tla's three workflows repurposed. Annex A disposes of every earlier Build
clause; Annex B lists seven dependent entries owed
The discussion of 2026.11.12; f1-tla at 5fe66dd
Drafted 2026.11.12 by the assistant at the custodian's
direction, not reviewed
Revision before ratification

Intake has gates of its own, and every class's vote opens on its own gates. New §3a: seven mechanical intake gates. IG-1 resolves digests; IG-2 checks every object has a complete line; IG-3 checks external pins, fetching where the upstream still serves the object; IG-4 reruns the extractor on the cited log positions for every

run object; IG-5 excludes payload; IG-6 checks labels only grow; IG-7 classifies, and an intake classified against a superseded root is refused at tally. §3a also declares the residual: no gate checks what data teaches. §3 I-3: the struck "The gates check only the manifest's form" is replaced. §6 gains G-4 and a gate table by class,

which finds no stated gate for mechanism code, profiles or seatings; those do not promote until one is written. §1's table, §12 (GatedIntake, OwnClassGates, gates for the three classes, the reference's refusals, the ADR-0024 §4 item), Options (four rows), Consequences, Open obligations, Annex A (ADR-0024, ADR-0026,
ADR-0034 rows), the header's debts and Annex B (item 8, ADR-0024 §4) follow
